key_insight: A neural network policy optimized by a genetic algorithm can learn minimum-time navigation in 2D flows and match or exceed optimal-control, Q-learning, and actor-critic baselines.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, parallelizable way to compute practical guidance policies for autonomous vehicles or micro-robots moving through complex fluid environments.
method: Parameterize the steering policy with a neural network
Evolve candidate policies with Darwinian selection and parameter mutation
Optimize for minimum travel time without crossover or reward shaping
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of analytical and numerical optimal-control solutions on benchmark cases, including two-dimensional turbulence, and better performance than Q-learning and one-step actor-critic.
watch_item: Robustness is limited when unresolved turbulent fluctuations become comparable to or larger than the vessel’s slip velocity.
paper_title: Learning minimum-time navigation policies in two-dimensional flows with a genetic algorithm
